purpose: Ensures the system technically enforces approved authorizations for logical access, so that users can only perform the actions their assigned permissions allow.
summary: The system enforces access control policy at the point of access (e.g., role-based access control, permission checks) rather than relying solely on procedural agreement not to exceed authorized access.
expectedStatementElements: What access control model is used (RBAC, ABAC, ACLs, etc.)
Who defines and approves the access rules/roles
How enforcement is verified (testing, logging of denied attempts)
How exceptions to standard access rules are handled and approved
evidenceExamples: Role/permission matrix showing enforced access levels
System configuration screenshots or exports showing enforcement mechanism
commonGaps: Statement describes policy but not the technical enforcement mechanism
No evidence that enforcement is actually tested or verified
interviewQuestions: What technical control actually blocks unauthorized access -- not just policy?
How would we verify enforcement is working today, not just configured once?
Who approves exceptions to standard role-based access?
